# Policy outline and common topics

## Outline for any policy

1. **Purpose.** Why the policy exists, in one or two sentences.
2. **Scope.** Who it covers (employees, contractors, locations) and who it does not.
3. **Policy.** The rules, in plain language and short sections.
4. **How to request, report or apply.** Steps, forms, who approves, timelines.
5. **Roles.** What employees, managers and HR each do.
6. **Exceptions.** Who can approve them and how.
7. **Related policies.**
8. **Owner and review date.**

Write for a reader who is busy and not a lawyer. Use the company's language setting.

## Common topics and what usually needs legal confirmation

| Topic | Typical contents | Confirm with legal for the jurisdiction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Leave and time off | Vacation, sick, parental, bereavement, public holidays | Minimum entitlements, carry-over, pay during leave |
| Working hours and overtime | Schedules, breaks, overtime approval | Limits, overtime pay rules, record keeping |
| Remote and hybrid work | Eligibility, equipment, security, working from another country | Tax and employment law when working abroad, expense rules |
| Code of conduct | Expected behavior, conflicts of interest, gifts | Whistleblower protections |
| Anti-harassment and anti-discrimination | Definitions, reporting channels, investigation steps, no retaliation | Mandatory procedures and committees (for example, internal committees required in some countries), training duties |
| Expenses and travel | What is covered, approval, receipts | Tax treatment |
| Data protection for employees | What employee data is collected and why | Privacy law duties, retention |
| Performance and conduct processes | Feedback, improvement plans | Disciplinary procedure rules, notice and appeal rights |
| Recruitment and equal opportunity | Fair hiring commitments, adjustments | Protected characteristics in each jurisdiction |

Never state a statutory number (days of leave, hours, notice periods) unless the user provided it or it is quoted from a document the user supplied. Mark it for legal instead.
